In 1939, Albert Einstein signed a letter that started the nuclear age. Two pages. Typed. Polite.

But here's what nobody tells you: that letter almost didn't make it to the President.

It sat for ten weeks. Hitler invaded Poland. And the scientists even thought about handing it to Charles Lindbergh.

When it finally reached Roosevelt, he said, according to the man who delivered it: "This requires action."

The action? About six thousand dollars. For the most important scientific warning of the century.

Fifteen years later, Einstein told a friend that signing it was the one great mistake of his life.

The full story, including the twist about the Germans, is on the channel. Before History Changed.
